items.headline: New models from Anthropic and OpenAI are arriving faster
items.dek:
you're not crazy

between anthropic and openai, a new model used to come out every ~10 weeks

now it's every ~11 days
items.author: josh :) (@jfonsecarivera)
items.caption: Scatter of each Anthropic (orange square) and OpenAI (green triangle) launch, 2024-2026: days since the previous launch by either lab, with a black rolling-median line from 70 days to 11 days and a grey middle-50% band.
items.notes: Image is the original (2048x1270) from pbs.twimg.com/media/HTZ4mB0aAAElOZE.jpg?name=orig. No data-source footnote on the chart. I reproduced its 35 markers from vendor pages (see datasets 'chart-marker-decode-vs-vendor-dates'); definition = major launches, see facts. Post: 344,785 views / 7,352 likes / 491 reposts / 146 quotes / 165 replies as of 2026-10-05. Author is an Anthropic safety fellow (bio) - disclose if citing.

datasets.title: Third-party count of distinct models released per year (unbenchmark.com 'AI Models Released Over Time by Lab', loaded 2026-10-05)
datasets.notes: AGTPinsights' post (https://x.com/AGTPinsights/status/2105100887047933962) quotes exactly these totals (15 / 42 / 39) and says the data was 'shared in the replies' to the original post; I could not read the replies, so I cannot confirm the chart author used this dataset (his chart plots gaps for only 35 major launches, not these 96 models).

facts.claim: Reproduced from primary sources, the chart's numbers hold for its own definition: median gap between consecutive major Anthropic/OpenAI launches was 70 days (10 weeks) for launches dated Jan-Jun 2024 and 10.5 days (the chart's '11') over Apr 5 - Oct 5 2026.
facts.source: Computed from vendor launch dates (anthropic.com pages; openai.com pages via Wayback; OpenAI API changelog). Arithmetic: Jan-Jun 2024 gaps = [104 (Claude 2.1 Nov 21 2023 -> Claude 3 Mar 4), 70 (-> GPT-4o May 13), 38 (-> Claude 3.5 Sonnet Jun 20)] -> median 70. Apr 5-Oct 5 2026 gaps = [33, 9, 7, 35, 12, 17, 4, 24, 39, 2, 19, 0, 6, 1] -> sorted [0, 1, 2, 4, 6, 7, 9, 12, 17, 19, 24, 33, 35, 39] -> median of 14 = (9+12)/2 = 10.5.

facts.claim: I could match all 35 launch markers in the chart image to vendor-announced launches: 34 detected by image analysis agree with the vendor dates within 1 day and the plotted gaps within 0.5 day; the 35th (o1, 2024-12-05, gap 44) is hidden under the median line. The chart's line starts at 70.0 and ends at 10.8 on my pixel read.
facts.source: Image analysis of the chart; vendor dates in releases_2024_2026.csv

facts.claim: The chart's set is 'major launches', not every model: it includes Sonnet-tier releases (Sonnet 4.6, 5, 5.5), GPT-4.1, GPT-5.3-Codex, the invitation-only Claude Mythos Preview and the GPT-5.6 limited preview (Jun 26), but omits Haiku, mini/nano, Instant, Pro, gpt-oss, Codex variants, image/audio/video models and cyber models.
facts.source: Chart marker decode vs vendor lists (releases_2024_2026.csv column in_chart_dots)

facts.claim: Flagship-only (the lab's headline model line at launch): median gap fell from 70 days (Jan-Jun 2024; gaps 104, 70, 38) to 14.5 days (Apr 5 - Oct 5 2026; 12 gaps), about 4.8x faster - roughly 10 weeks to 2 weeks, not 11 days. Public-access-only flagships: 70 -> 15 days.

Counting every named model launch (including mini/Haiku, Codex, cyber, image, audio, video and open-weight models), the median gap fell from 39 days (Jan-Jun 2024, 5 gaps) to 5 days (Apr 5 - Oct 5 2026, 26 gaps): about 8x faster. Adding dated snapshots, announced-only previews and Epoch research models gives 19.5 -> 5 days.
facts.source: Computed. Jan-Jun 2024 all-launch gaps = [65, 39, 9, 61, 38] -> median 39. Last-6-month gaps (26) -> median 5.

facts.claim: Epoch AI's independent model database gives the same direction: median gap between Anthropic/OpenAI language-model publications 36 days (Jan-Jun 2024) -> 12 days (Apr 5 - Oct 5 2026); counting all Epoch-tracked Anthropic/OpenAI models (incl. image, speech, video) 21 -> 6 days.
facts.source: Epoch AI all_ai_models.csv, distinct publication dates, computed.

facts.claim: Within a single lab the cadence is slower than the headline: over Apr 5 - Oct 5 2026 the median gap between Anthropic's major launches was 21 days (9 gaps) and between OpenAI's was 49 days (5 gaps); the combined '11 days' comes from interleaving two labs.
facts.source: Computed from the chart set. Anthropic gaps [49, 9, 42, 12, 21, 24, 39, 21, 6]; OpenAI gaps [49, 64, 69, 19, 7].

facts.claim: The '10 weeks' start is fragile: it rests on only three gaps. Adding OpenAI's GPT-4 Turbo with Vision general-availability release (2024-04-09) to the chart's set changes the Jan-Jun 2024 median from 70 to 37 days (gaps 104, 36, 34, 38).
facts.source: Computed; OpenAI API changelog 'Apr 9: Released GPT-4 Turbo with Vision in general availability in the API'

facts.claim: The '11 days' end is moderately robust: using GPT-5.6's public date (Jul 9) instead of the Jun 26 limited preview leaves the median at 10.5; also dropping the invitation-only Mythos Preview gives 12; dropping the two Sonnet launches in the window (Sonnet 5 and 5.5) gives 14.5; the median over the last 90 days (Jul 7 - Oct 5) is 6 days.
facts.source: Computed (sensitivity runs on the chart set)

facts.claim: Same-day and near-simultaneous launches are common: Claude Opus 4.6 and GPT-5.3-Codex both launched 2026-02-05; Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Sol/Luna both 2026-09-22; Claude Opus 4.1 and gpt-oss 2025-08-05; Sonnet 5.5 (Sep 28) and GPT-6.1 Sol (Sep 29) were one day apart.
facts.source: anthropic.com/news (Sep 22 and Sep 28 2026 items); OpenAI API changelog (Sep 22, Sep 29 2026)

facts.claim: Launches per half-year (chart's major-launch set, 2024 H1 ... 2026 H1): 3, 3, 5, 6, 11, then 7 in the 97 days of 2026 H2 so far (a pace of about 13 per 184 days). All named model launches: 5, 8, 16, 17, 22, then 12 in 97 days (a pace of about 23 per 184 days).

Anthropic's own system-card index lists 19 release entries from 'Claude 3, March 2024' to 'Claude Opus 5.5, September 2026' (it omits Claude 3 Haiku, Claude Gov and the newest Sonnet 5.5, which I list from the newsroom); the newsroom shows Claude Sonnet 5.5 on Sep 28, Claude Opus 5.5 on Sep 22 and Claude Fable 5.1 / Mythos 5.1 on Sep 1, 2026.

Post by josh :) (@jfonsecarivera, 'safety fellow @AnthropicAI'), Sep 29 2026: "you're not crazy

between anthropic and openai, a new model used to come out every ~10 weeks

now it's every ~11 days" - 344,785 views, 7,352 likes as of Oct 5 2026.

not_found.searched: api.fxtwitter.com status + thread endpoints (no replies returned); post text; AGTPinsights summary; unbenchmark.com data pages. AGTPinsights says data from unbenchmark.com was 'shared in the replies' but replies were not readable. I instead reconstructed the 35-launch set by decoding the chart's markers (all matched vendor dates).

openai.com/index/* returns Cloudflare 403/'Just a moment' to curl, WebFetch and the headless browser; dates were read from Wayback (web.archive.org id_ copies) of the vendor pages instead, plus the OpenAI API changelog. GPT-5.6 (openai.com/index/gpt-5-6/) and GPT-5.5 pages could not be re-read in the last attempts; their dates rest on the changelog, TechCrunch, Wikipedia, Epoch and (GPT-5.5) an earlier successful Wayback read ('April 23, 2026').
